docs.title: Multistage Approval Workflows and Activity Inbox

sections.text: The native **Approvals** application lets organizations enforce multi-step governance over sensitive write and destructive ERP operations—such as confirming high-value orders, posting entries, or approving automated agent actions—while giving every internal user a clear **Requests** inbox to review, track, and audit decisions. > **Installation note**: **Approvals** ships as a native addon (approvals). Administrators can install it from the module manager or via CLI (--install approvals). Once installed, clicking **Approvals** in the sidebar opens directly on **Approvals Overview**, alongside **Requests** (for internal users) and **Workflows** (for administrators).

* **Internal User (base.group_user)**: Opens **Approvals → Requests** to act on pending requests assigned to their user or group, monitor requests they submitted (**My requests**), and review completed decision history (**Reviewed**). * **Settings Administration (base.group_system)**: Opens **Approvals → Workflows** to design draft workflows, define ordered review steps and eligible reviewers, publish immutable revisions, and archive or reactivate workflows.

Administrators define which operations require approval and who must review each stage under **Approvals → Workflows**: 1. Open **Approvals → Workflows** and click **New** to create a workflow in **Draft** state. 2. Enter a clear **Workflow name** (for example, *Purchase order approval* or *Vendor payment release*). 3. Under **Applies to**, choose the scope: * **Company**: Limit the workflow to one company, or leave blank (**All companies**) to apply database-wide. * **Requester type**: Choose whether the workflow governs **User** actions or delegated **Agent** actions. 4. Under **Operation**, select what triggers the workflow: * **Operation effect**: Choose **Write** (state-changing business actions) or **Destructive** (cancellations, deletions, or high-impact reversals). * **Model**: Choose the target ERP model (for example, Purchase Order or Journal Entry), or leave blank for **All models**. * **Method**: Pick an exposed operation from the live searchable **Method** selector (filtered automatically to methods matching the selected model and operation effect). 5. Open the **Review steps** tab and add between 1 and 16 ordered stages: * **Order (sequence)**: Controls the exact execution order (Stage 1 must approve before Stage 2 becomes actionable). * **Step name**: Descriptive label shown to reviewers (for example, *Department Manager*, *Finance Review*, *Director Sign-off*). * **Eligible reviewers**: Assign specific **Users** (active internal users) and/or **Groups** permitted to decide that stage. 6. Click **Save**, then click **Publish** to activate the workflow.

Published workflows are backed by immutable policy revisions so completed and in-flight audit trails can never be altered retroactively: * **Draft → Active (Publish)**: Locks the workflow definition and starts intercepting matching operations immediately. * **Updating an Active Workflow (Create revision → Publish revision)**: Open an active or archived workflow and click **Create revision** to clone it into an editable draft linked to the prior policy. Adjust steps or reviewers, then click **Publish revision**. Confirming archives the old revision and expires any incomplete requests under the superseded revision. * **Pausing or Retiring (Archive / Activate)**: Click **Archive** on an active workflow to stop intercepting new operations (and expire incomplete requests). Archived workflows can be restored later via **Activate**.

Every internal user manages their approval queue under **Approvals → Requests**: 1. **Switch Queue Filters**: * **To review** *(default)*: Displays pending requests currently at a stage where you (or one of your groups) are an eligible reviewer. * **My requests**: Displays approval requests initiated by your own operations so you can track which stage is currently reviewing them. * **Reviewed**: Displays requests you have already decided or completed. 2. Open any request to inspect the read-only **Approval request** form: * **Request**: Request identifier, **Requested by**, **Companies**, and **Expires** timestamp. * **Progress**: Current **Status** (Pending, Approved, Executed, Denied, or Expired), **Current stage**, **Total stages**, and **Review stage** name. * **Approval stages** tab: Full stage-by-stage audit log showing who decided each stage and when. * **Technical details** tab: **Target model**, **Operation**, **Payload SHA-256** digest, and **Execution receipt** once executed. 3. For a pending request where you are authorized to decide, choose an action in the header: * **Approve**: Advances the request to the next review stage (or executes the approved operation automatically after the final stage approves). * **Deny**: Rejects the request after confirmation; the guarded operation is not executed.

* **Cannot Edit a Published Workflow**: Published workflows are intentionally read-only for audit integrity. Click **Create revision** to make changes safely, then **Publish revision**. * **Approve / Deny Buttons Not Shown**: Confirm the request status is still **Pending**, you belong to the eligible **Users** or **Groups** for the **Current stage**, and the request has not expired. * **Stage or Digest Mismatch Notice**: ERPForAll binds every approval decision to the exact stage number and **Payload SHA-256** digest. If another reviewer already decided the stage or a new revision expired the request, reload the request to see its latest state.
